subject: Follow-up: pricing & commitment options for StreamlineAI - token volumes and discounts
messages:
From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Park <jamie@streamlineai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 14:05:00 -0800
Subject: Follow-up: pricing & commitment options for StreamlineAI - token volumes and discounts

Hi Jamie / Priya —

Great to meet yesterday. Quick recap + a few asks so we can put a clean pricing proposal on paper:

Summary from call:
- Product: real-time summarization + search augmentation for enterprise customers (ML-infused UX).
- Current expected baseline: ~50M tokens/month initially.
- Anticipated peak months (on heavy onboarding): up to ~250M tokens.
- Primary model needs: low-latency generation for short responses (~200–600 tokens per request).

Questions we still need answered to finalize numbers:
1) Can you confirm the 50M baseline and 250M peak tokens, or provide a range for next 12 months?
2) What is your budget range for inference (monthly)? Helpful to see a target $/1M tokens you are aiming for so we can map discount tiers to your unit-econ goals.
3) Are you eligible for a startup program (YC/Techstars/seed/Series A)? If so, we may be able to apply credits + an introductory discount.

What I can do next:
- Draft 2 pricing options for you: (A) pay-as-you-go (no commit) and (B) committed-use (6–24 month tiers) showing $/1M token unit cost and monthly spend at your baseline/peak.
- Call out how startup credits would layer on (if eligible) and the net-first-90-days cost.

If you can reply with Q1 answers (especially the budget target $/1M and startup eligibility) I’ll get a tailored one-pager and workbook over to you by EOD Thursday.

Attaching a blank pricing workbook and SOW template for transparency.

Thanks —
Vivek
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: pricing-workbook-StreamlineAI.xlsx] [Attachment: SOW-template.docx]

From: Jamie Park <jamie@streamlineai.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@vcfund.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: pricing & commitment options for StreamlineAI - token volumes and discounts

Hi Vivek —

Thanks for the recap — confirmed on most of this. A few clarifications:
- Baseline: expect 40–60M tokens/month for the next 3 months as we pilot with 3 customers.
- Q2–Q3 ramp: if product-market fit holds, we expect month-on-month growth leading to 200–300M tokens in peak months (we modeled a 6–9 month ramp).
- Budget: right now we have a central inference budget of $10k–$20k/month during pilot; if we land two larger customers we can expand to $30k–$50k/month.
- Unit target: we’re shooting for ~$15–$30 per 1M tokens depending on SLA and throughput. Lower is obviously better in the long-term, but we need predictable latency.

Startup eligibility: we closed a pre-seed (~$2.5M) in 2025 and are YC Alumni (Batch 2024) — happy to send YC docs if that helps.

Next step for us is to see a short proposal that translates the 50M baseline and 250M peak into monthly cost at both pay-as-you-go and committed tiers. Also interested in any multi-year incentives or credits you can offer for early-stage startups.

Cheers,
Jamie Park
Head of Product
StreamlineAI
[Attachment: StreamlineAI-cap-table.pdf]

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
To: Jamie Park <jamie@streamlineai.com>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 07:58:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: pricing & commitment options for StreamlineAI - token volumes and discounts

Jamie —

Thanks for the quick clarifications and congrats on the pre-seed + YC — that qualifies you for our startup intake. I put together two clear options below so you can pick the right path based on how you prioritize cash vs predictability/discount.

Option A — Pay-as-you-go (no commit)
- List unit price: $35 per 1M tokens for production LLMs (includes autoscaling + 99th-pctl latency tiers).
- Example math at baseline (50M tokens): 50 * $35 = $1,750/month.
- Pros: flexible, no long-term commitment; Cons: higher unit cost during spikes.

Option B — Committed-use (preferred for predictable unit economics)
- 6-month commit (min 500M total): 12% discount off list
- 12-month commit (min 1B total): 22% discount off list
- 24-month commit (min 2B total): 30% discount off list
- Example math at baseline (50M/month) using 12-month commit: effective unit = $35 * (1 - 0.22) = $27.30 per 1M -> 50 * $27.30 = $1,365/month.

Startup intake layering
- YC alumni: one-time credit of $15k applied to first bill + an additional 10% introductory discount for first 90 days.
- If StreamlineAI signs a 12M committed-use agreement, we can additionally offer a 5% accelerator credit (applied as bill credit over the first 6 months).

Multi-year incentive note
- For deals that include growth-based escalation commitments (e.g., 2x volume growth targets with guaranteed mins), we can structure stepped discounts that increase as you hit milestones. That’s generally how we enable multi-year economics while protecting capacity.

Next steps I propose:
1) I’ll upload a short proposal PDF and a populated pricing workbook that shows your baseline & peak scenarios (attached).
2) If the 12-month commit looks reasonable, we can draft an MSA + SOW and run legal review — I’ll include lauren for commercial terms and ben for onboarding timelines.

Would you like me to show a version that nets-in the YC credits so you can see the first 90 days spend?

Best,
Vivek
Director, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
[Attachment: RWD-proposal-StreamlineAI-v1.pdf]

From: Jamie Park <jamie@streamlineai.com>
To: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek@redwood.ai>
Cc: Priya Shah <priya@vcfund.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 12 Feb 2026 09:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Follow-up: pricing & commitment options for StreamlineAI - token volumes and discounts

Vivek / Lauren —

This is helpful, thanks. Yes please: send the net-in YC-credit view so I can show the CFO. At a glance the 12-month commit + YC credit looks interesting.

A few follow-ups:
- Can you confirm whether the committed discounts apply to both hosted and dedicated variants (we may want dedicated for a later tier)?
- What is your SLA for 99th-pctl latency on the production LLM path used in these examples?
- Can you add an appendix with standard contract terms around data retention and audit logs (our security team will ask).

If those answers look good I’ll ask legal to fast-track review once we have an MSA. Priya — looping you so the fund can see the proposed structure.

Thanks —
Jamie
Head of Product, StreamlineAI
